evidence.quote: requirements on operators of websites

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends the COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312), governing operators of child-directed and actual-knowledge services collecting personal information from children under 13. Effective June 23, 2025; regulated entities have until April 22, 2026 to comply, except specified provisions.
summary.long: The amended Rule updates the Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule (16 CFR Part 312), which governs operators of websites and online services directed to, or with actual knowledge of collecting personal information from, children under 13. It adds mobile telephone numbers to 'online contact information' for limited use to send text messages to parents to obtain parental consent, and adds government-issued identifiers and biometric identifiers that can be used for automated recognition of an individual to 'personal information'. It defines 'mixed audience website or online service', clarifies that persistent identifiers used for support for internal operations may be used for those activities, and modifies operators' direct and online notice, information security, deletion and retention obligations, and the annual assessment, disclosure and reporting duties of FTC-approved Safe Harbor programs. A 'text plus' verifiable parental consent method is added. The Commission declined to adopt proposed changes on ed tech and school authorization, removal of 'directly' from the third-party provision, screen and user names, engagement prompts, and an audience-analysis exemption. Effective June 23, 2025; compliance by April 22, 2026, except § 312.11(d)(1), (d)(4) and (g).

notes: Part 1 of 3 covers the Overview, Background and Statement of Basis and Purpose through the start of the discussion of section 312.4(c)(1). Operative regulatory text is in later parts, so no obligations, thresholds or events are coded here. Effective date June 23, 2025; compliance date April 22, 2026, except section 312.11(d)(1), (d)(4) and (g). Footnote 9 reads changing 'website' to 'website', an apparent typo for 'Web site'. Entities listed are firms named in cited enforcement footnotes, not addressees; the Rule's addressees ('operators') are generic and not named. Part 2 of 3 is Federal Register preamble (discussion of comments and Commission decisions on §§ 312.4 to 312.10), not the codified regulatory text; no obligations or thresholds are coded from it. The statutory basis (COPPA) appears here only as 'the COPPA statute'; no enabling-act citation is given in this part. Internal points: the preamble drops 'the nature of' from the integral-disclosure phrase in §§ 312.4(c)(1)(iv) and 312.5(a)(2), but footnote 326 uses 'integral to the website or online service' as adopted; the Commission declines the § 312.5(c)(4) engagement-prompt amendment and does not define 'activity' in § 312.7. Commenter organisations are not coded as entities. Part 3 covers preamble Parts II.G to V (retention, safe harbor programs, NPRM questions, PRA, RFA, other matters) and the republished regulatory text of 16 CFR Part 312, §§ 312.1 to 312.13. Preamble commenters (e.g., CARU, kidSAFE, ESRB) are not coded as entities. Operators and approved safe harbor programs are class addressees, not named entities; their duties belong in the obligation rows. Target instrument IDs are empty because no registry IDs were supplied. Internal points: footnote 604 says the 2024 NPRM inadvertently omitted the final sentence of § 312.11(b)(2), which the final text keeps. The PRA section gives OMB approval through April 30, 2025, while footnote 671 says the 2024 NPRM wrongly stated March 31, 2025. Most amended requirements take effect with a 365-day compliance period from publication; §§ 312.11(d)(1), (d)(4) and (g) state fixed dates of October 22, 2025 and July 21, 2025.

obligations.summary: Operators of mixed audience websites or online services must determine whether a visitor is a child in a neutral manner that does not default to a set age or encourage falsifying age information.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies when an operator determines whether a visitor is a child, under the mixed audience definition.

evidence.provision: § 312.2 (definition of Mixed audience website or online service)
evidence.quote: Any collection of age information, or other means of determining whether a visitor is a child, must be done in a neutral manner that does not default to a set age or encourage visitors to falsify age information.

obligations.summary: Operators of websites or online services directed to children, or with actual knowledge of collecting personal information from a child, may not collect such information in a manner that violates the regulations in this part.

evidence.quote: It shall be unlawful for any operator of a website or online service directed to children

obligations.summary: Operators must provide notice and obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting, using or disclosing children's personal information; the section also requires direct notice to parents, the content of direct and online notices, and posting of the online notice with the data retention policy.

evidence.quote: It shall be the obligation of the operator to provide notice and obtain verifiable parental consent prior to collecting, using, or disclosing personal information from children.

obligations.summary: Operators must obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting, using or disclosing children's personal information, including material changes; must make reasonable efforts using accepted consent methods; and must give parents the option to consent without consenting to third-party disclosure unless integral.

evidence.quote: An operator is required to obtain verifiable parental consent before any collection, use, or disclosure of personal information from children

obligations.summary: On a parent's request, operators must provide a description of the personal information collected from the child, the opportunity to refuse further use or collection and to direct deletion, and a means of reviewing the child's information, verifying the requestor is a parent.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies upon request of a parent whose child has provided personal information.

evidence.quote: the operator of that website or online service is required to provide to that parent the following

obligations.summary: Operators may not condition a child's participation in a game, prize or other activity on disclosing more personal information than is reasonably necessary to participate.

evidence.quote: prohibited from conditioning a child

obligations.summary: Operators must establish and maintain reasonable procedures and a written information security program with designated coordinators, at least annual risk assessments, safeguards, regular testing and at least annual evaluation; before sharing children's information with other operators, service providers or third parties, they must take reasonable steps and obtain written assurances.

evidence.quote: The operator must establish and maintain reasonable procedures to protect the confidentiality, security, and integrity of personal information collected from children.

obligations.summary: Operators must retain children's personal information online only as long as reasonably necessary for the specific purposes collected, must delete it when no longer reasonably necessary using reasonable measures, and may not retain it indefinitely.

evidence.quote: An operator of a website or online service shall retain personal information collected online from a child for only as long as is reasonably necessary

obligations.summary: Operators must establish, implement and maintain a written data retention policy setting out the purposes of collection, the business need for retention and a deletion timeframe, and must provide it in the online notice.

evidence.quote: At a minimum, the operator must establish, implement, and maintain a written data retention policy
